olivia (acme): Hey team — our org hit 429s this morning, but our billing page still shows 0 credits used. Credits should have refreshed for our account at local midnight but they didn't. Any ideas?

maya-cs: Sorry about that — can you paste the tenant id and one example request id/timestamp so we can trace?

olivia (acme): Tenant: org_9X3b. Example API response: 429, body: {\"error\":\"quota_exceeded\"}, headers: \`X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0\`, \`X-RateLimit-Reset: 2054107200\`. Request ts: 2054109901. We are in America/Chicago (CST).

ops-bot: Alert: org_9X3b exceeded monthly quota (auto-block) at 2054109901. Created ticket #C-7832.

jordan-eng: Thanks — looking. Quick clarification: when you say "billing page shows 0 credits used" do you mean the UI shows "available: 0" or it shows the meter at 100% used?

olivia (acme): The meter shows available: 0 but the timeline indicates usage 0 for the new cycle (it looks like it didn't roll). We definitely had heavy usage before reset window.

leo-sre: From past incidents, two usual causes: 1) reset boundary executed in UTC but UI shows tenant local tz, causing perceived mismatch; 2) a cache race where the tenant's quota object in Redis didn't flip at reset and some nodes continued to serve stale remaining counts.

jordan-eng: Can you run this quick repro so we have the exact header dump?

olivia (acme): Sure — here's a curl from earlier: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_XXX" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2026 05:05:01 GMT
X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d
X-RateLimit-Limit-Month: 1000000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 2054107200
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"quota_exceeded","message":"monthly quota exhausted"}
```

maya-cs: Thanks — that reset header (2054107200) converts to Tue Oct 12 00:00:00 UTC. Your tenant timezone (America/Chicago) was at 7pm previous day when UTC rolled. That explains the mismatch in the UI vs API-block timing, but doesn't explain why the UI meter shows 0 usage for the new cycle.

leo-sre: I pulled logs for org_9X3b around 2054107000-2054110000. I see the monthly-roll job executed at 2054107200 (UTC) and wrote new quota objects to the DB, but there was a transient Redis auth error on two caching nodes at 2054107215-2054107230. Some API servers continued serving using an older in-memory quota snapshot until they rotated configs (~2054112000). That would cause the behavior you saw: some requests were blocked immediately (nodes that saw new 0 remaining), others still used stale counts (UI read from primary DB showed reset but cache reads returned old values).

jordan-eng: Root cause: cache failover + inconsistent propagation window during the UTC reset. Action plan: (1) manual force-sync the affected tenant caches, (2) deploy a small change to make reset write be atomic (DB write + cache invalidation) with retry on redis auth errors, (3) add a telemetry counter for "quota-reset-propagation-lag".

maya-cs: Olivia — immediate mitigation: we can force-reset your tenant quotas now which will unblock calls and adjust the UI to reflect correct usage. Do you want us to do that now?

olivia (acme): Yes please, unblock now — our product is down for a feature flag rollback until this clears.

leo-sre: Running force-reset script now (idempotent). Command: 
```
# force-reset for org_9X3b
scripts/force_reset_quota.sh org_9X3b --dry-run=false
```

ops-bot: Run log: force-reset job started by leo-sre at 2054110200, completed at 2054110222. Affected nodes: 5.

maya-cs: Confirming: olivia, can you try a request?

olivia (acme): Retried — 200 OK, tokens deducted, UI now shows usage for new cycle. Thank you! :tada:

jordan-eng: For tracking, filing a follow-up engineering ticket to harden reset: ENG-1294. We'll schedule a hotfix to add the retry/invalidation within the next 48 hours and a postmortem note.

leo-sre: Also adding a dashboard panel for "quota-reset-propagation-lag" and an alert when >30s for any tenant.

maya-cs: Closing the customer-facing loop: olivia, we'll keep you posted when ENG-1294 ships. If you want us to schedule a monthly runbook check for your org's resets (until fix ships), we can.

olivia (acme): Appreciate it. A runbook check would be great for the next two cycles. Thanks everyone. :pray:

billing-bot: Note: manual force-reset performed; billing records unchanged (no retroactive credit). If you need a billing adjustment please open a billing ticket. https://docs.redwood.ai/billing/credits

jordan-eng: (internal) Postmortem memo to draft: timeline, cache auth failure root cause, mitigation plan, and customer outreach.

maya-cs: Marking thread resolved for support; leaving open for ENG until ENG-1294 closes. :white_check_mark:
